sections.title: Will my land get CLU? The 3-minute answer
sections.html: What decides it, what it costs, how long it takes, and how we handle the file.

sections.title: What you need to know first

items.title: Do I need CLU?
items.html: Yes, if you want to use land in a planned area for something other than its approved use, such as farmland for a factory or warehouse.

items.title: Will my land get it?
items.html:
It depends on three things: the area plan, the road and your unit.

Three things decide it

items.title: Is my plot the right size?
items.html:
Usually, yes. Most zones have no minimum area.

The rules

items.title: Does the road matter?
items.html: Yes. On farmland you need at least a 20 ft link road or a 33 ft rasta.

items.title: What will it cost?
items.html:
An application fee of ₹10 per sq m, then charges set by your area. We work them out for your plot.

Cost and time

items.title: How long before I can build?
items.html: In an industrial zone, a decision is due within 60 days of a complete file.

items.title: How long do I have once I get it?
items.html: Two years to build, and it can be renewed.

sections.outro_html: Rules last checked 17 October 2026, including government amendments up to 14 September 2026.

sections.title: CLU done for businesses like yours.
Will your land work for your unit? Three things decide it.

items.title: What the area plan allows here
items.html: Every planned area has a development plan. It marks land as industrial, farmland or transport zone, and grades the nearby town by growth potential.

items.title: The road to your plot
items.html: On farmland you need an existing village link road at least 20 ft wide, a revenue or panchayat road at least 33 ft wide, or direct highway frontage with the road authority's permission. You can make your own 33 ft rasta by donating a strip of land to the gram panchayat, before you apply. In an industrial zone, the minimum is a 33 ft road linked to the sector road.

items.title: How polluting your unit is
items.html: The state pollution board puts every activity in a category: white, green, orange or red. White, green and orange units can get CLU on farmland. Red-category units need a plot in an industrial zone.

sections.outro_html:
Your neighbour's CLU doesn't mean you'll get one. Their zone, their road and their date were their own.

sections.title: Know your costs and timeline upfront.
sections.html:
No surprises: we work out what applies to your plot before you commit.

WHAT YOU PAY

Government charges, set by your area

An application fee of ₹10 per sq m, then conversion charges, plus development charges in some areas.

Ways to pay less

MSMEs in less-developed blocks pay half the conversion charges, and several sectors pay half the development charges.

Warehouse or logistics park?

Part of the development charges can be reimbursed once you start operations.

HOW LONG IT TAKES

60 days, once your file is complete

For plots in an industrial zone, that's the legal limit for a decision. Farmland cases aren't bound by it.

HOW LONG IT LASTS

Two years to build, renewable

For sites up to 25 acres: time to build and start using the land. You can renew it if you need longer.

articles.title: Change of Land Use (CLU) in Haryana: rules, charges and process
articles.content:
Whether your land can take a factory, what CLU costs, the papers you'll need and how long the permission lasts. Taken from TCP Haryana's current policies for industrial proposals in controlled areas.

Can my land get CLU?

In an industrial zone, all unit types are allowed, with no minimum area, subject to pollution clearance. In the agriculture zone, it depends on the nearest town and how close you are to it. Red-category units can't get CLU there.

What does it cost?

A scrutiny fee of ₹10 per sq m with the application, then conversion charges and, in some areas, development charges, demanded in the Letter of Intent (LOI).

How long does it last?

Two years to put the land to use, for sites up to 25 acres other than multi-storey buildings. It can be renewed.

Who grants it?

The Department of Town and Country Planning (TCP), Haryana, for land in controlled areas. Land inside municipal limits follows the urban local body's route; check which applies to yours.

Can your land take a factory?

These rules cover industrial proposals in TCP-controlled areas. They depend on the zone your land is in on the development plan, and on the potential of the nearest town. Most industrial CLU has no minimum area.

Zone on the development planHyper or high potential townMedium potential townLow potential town
Industrial zoneAll units, no area limit, subject to pollution clearanceThe sameThe same
Agriculture zone, within 2 km of the urbanisable zoneNot allowedGreen, white and orange units, up to 5 acresGreen, white and orange units, any area
Agriculture zone, beyond 2 kmNot allowedGreen, white and orange units, any areaGreen, white and orange units, any area
Transport and communication zoneWhite, green and orange units, at least 0.5 acre, within 25% of the zone's net planned areaThe sameThe same

The colour is your unit's pollution category. Red-category units can't get CLU in the agriculture zone.

Plot in an HSIIDC estate? You don't need CLU. Your building plans are filed with HSIIDC under the estate's rules. Pollution consents, the fire NOC and the factory licence still apply.

HSIIDC estate approvals ↗

Check my plot →

Does your road qualify?

ILLUSTRATIVE

  • PLOT Not an approved plot. ↕ 20 ft Existing village link road
  • PLOT Not an approved plot. ↕ 33 ft Revenue or panchayati rasta

Road width is one check. The zone, access permissions and your unit also matter.

  • Agriculture zone: at least a 20 ft existing village link road, or a 33 ft revenue or self-made panchayati rasta. Direct access from a national highway, scheduled road or state highway also qualifies once you have access permission.
  • A self-made panchayati rasta must be land donated to the gram panchayat before you apply, leading to a road of at least 33 ft.
  • Transport and communication zone: at least a 33 ft revenue rasta or public road, plus access from a planned 18 or 24 m internal road or a 12 m service road.
  • Industrial zone: at least a 33 ft road, with access from the sector road network. The frontage is widened and donated.

Access from a highway needs its own permission:

NHAI access NOC ↗ · PWD access NOC ↗

What CLU costs, and when you pay.

ChargeWhen you payWhat decides it
Scrutiny feeWith the application₹10 per sq m
Conversion chargesBy the date in the Letter of Intent (LOI)Rates set for your area. MSMEs pay half in B, C and D category blocks
External development charges (EDC)By the date in the LOIOnly for sites inside the urbanisable zone. Half for MSMEs and some sectors in B, C and D blocks, for new cases
Internal development charges (IDC)By the date in the LOIOnly where the site is in a developed sector

None of these is the price of the land.

Work out my charges →

The papers you'll need.

  • The sizra (aks-shajra), showing your plot, its road and the road's width
  • The latest jamabandi, signed by the patwari
  • Every mutation (intkal) entry for the land
  • The registry, sale deed or lease deed
  • The landowners' KYC and net-worth certificate
  • A non-encumbrance certificate from the tehsildar
  • Your Udyam registration, if you have one
  • The business's constitution document, and an authority letter or board resolution
  • Photos of the site

How a CLU application moves.

  1. Land and project checked. The zone, the road and your unit's pollution category.
  2. Papers collected and verified against the revenue record.
  3. The application prepared: the CLU-I form, site plan, utilisation plan and project report.
  4. Submission. Filed online through Invest Haryana, and the department's queries answered.
  5. Letter of Intent (LOI). It sets the charges, the conditions and a date to meet them. You sign the undertaking by OTP. It isn't the CLU permission yet.
  6. Compliance, then the CLU letter. Once the charges are paid and the conditions met, you sign the final form (CLU-II) by OTP and the CLU letter is issued.

Submission → Letter of Intent → Compliance → CLU letter

How long each step takes depends on your file and the department's queue. Haryana sets time limits for approvals under its Right to Service rules.

How long a CLU lasts.

Your siteTime to put the land to use
Up to 25 acres, not a multi-storey buildingTwo years
Up to 25 acres, multi-storeyThree years
25 acres or moreFive years
  • Renewal, for sites up to 25 acres that aren't multi-storey: up to three more years, on paying 10% of the current conversion charges.
  • One further year with government approval, if the delay was beyond your control, at 15% of the conversion charges.

What holds a CLU file up.

  • The road's width and name not shown on the sizra
  • Mutation entries not checked with the patwari
  • A jamabandi or non-encumbrance certificate without the patwari's or tehsildar's signature
  • The activity described loosely in the application
  • The wrong pollution category

Get my file checked →

Want it handled?

We check your plot, prepare the file and see it through to the CLU letter.

See our CLU service ↗

After the CLU letter.

The CLU letter confirms the permitted land use. Before construction, get the building plan approval and the Consent to Establish. Once the building is complete come the occupation certificate and the Consent to Operate.
